cultures.headline: Do not haggle with your beloved as you would over linen.
cultures.paragraph: Your beloved and what you have buried pull at each other, and Thoth records it to the hair. An old grievance is aired anew. Isis leans on the balance, and the scribe of the hall notes where it settles. Past Isis and Osiris, in the next court, Khonsu bars the door against Amun: your moods and your patrons each want it all. Leave the household accounts for another night.

cultures.headline: Wanting it badly is no reason to ask Aphrodite for it.
cultures.paragraph: Your desire and your hidden wealth cross each other, and the tripod answers at once. Someone digs up what you buried. Aphrodite throws the golden apple onto the table, and three guests stop speaking. At a lesser shrine than the one Aphrodite and Plouton share, Selene holds the far end of the agora against Zeus: your household and your standing with the powerful give opposite answers. Wait a day before you ask for what you want.

cultures.headline: Do not swear a vow of love at the standing stone in the middle of a fight.
cultures.paragraph: Your love and your family's land block each other at the gate, and the elders mark the day. An old loss bites again. Attart draws her sword at the feast, and the cups go down. In the fields beyond Attart and Motu, Yarikh convenes the council against Baal Hadad: your kin at home and your harvest pull the household two ways. Let the argument end before either of you speaks of love.

cultures.headline: Affection you paid for in shekels does not stay bought.
cultures.paragraph: Your pleasure fund and the debts you inherited undercut each other, entered without a correction. An old debt grows new interest. Astarte recalls the fleet halfway out, and the crews want their pay. On the page facing Astarte and Mot, Tanit demands a price of Baal Hammon: your household accounts and your profits compete for the same coin. Keep your purse shut until the week's books close.

cultures.headline: Keep courtship out of forum business.
cultures.paragraph: Your courtship and your inheritance obstruct each other, and the pontiff marks it in the calendar. An old family claim blocks your way. Venus quarrels with the bride's mother over the match, and the wedding is postponed. Below the Capitol, where Venus meets Dis Pater, Luna sits on the opposite bench from Iuppiter: your household affairs and your run for office pull in different directions. Let the courtship rest a week.
